english: For a real number $t$, let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$ and let $\{t\}=t-[t]$. For a real number $a$, consider the relation $R_a=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}:\ x=2[y]+3\{y\}-a\{y\}^{2}\right\}$. Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $a$ for which $R_a$ defines $y$ as a function of $x$, that is, for which every vertical line meets $R_a$ in at most one point. If $S=[\alpha,\beta]$, then the value of $\beta-\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: किसी वास्तविक संख्या $t$ के लिए, $[t]$ उस महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है जो $t$ से छोटा या उसके बराबर है तथा $\{t\}=t-[t]$ है। किसी वास्तविक संख्या $a$ के लिए संबंध $R_a=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}:\ x=2[y]+3\{y\}-a\{y\}^{2}\right\}$ पर विचार कीजिए। माना कि $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $a$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $R_a$ द्वारा $y$, $x$ का एक फलन परिभाषित होता है, अर्थात् प्रत्येक ऊर्ध्वाधर रेखा $R_a$ को अधिकतम एक बिन्दु पर मिलती है। यदि $S=[\alpha,\beta]$ है, तो $\beta-\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Vertical line test inside one block ($n$ fixed): $\varphi$ must be one-one on $[0,1)$. Since $\varphi'(0)=3>0$, $\varphi$ must stay increasing: $\varphi'(t)=3-2at\ge0$ for $t<1$ $\Rightarrow a\le\dfrac32$ (for $a>\dfrac32$, $\varphi$ rises then falls before $t=1$ and repeats values)
For $a\le\dfrac32$, block $n$ gives $x\in[2n,\ 2n+3-a)$ and block $n+1$ starts at $2n+2$
Blocks disjoint $\Leftrightarrow 2n+3-a\le 2n+2\Leftrightarrow a\ge1$ (for $a<1$ the value $x=2n+2$ comes from two values of $y$)
solution_full: Every real $y$ is uniquely $y=n+t$ with $n=[y]\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $t=\{y\}\in[0,1)$. Then $(x,y)\in R_a$ means $x=2n+\varphi(t)$ with $\varphi(t)=3t-at^{2}$.

$R_a$ defines $y$ as a function of $x$ exactly when the map $y\mapsto 2[y]+3\{y\}-a\{y\}^{2}$ is one-one on $\mathbb{R}$ (each vertical line $x=c$ then meets $R_a$ at most once). Two things are needed: $\varphi$ is one-one on $[0,1)$ (no repetition inside a block), and the sets of values of different blocks do not overlap.

Inside a block: $\varphi$ is a quadratic in $t$ with $\varphi'(t)=3-2at$ and $\varphi'(0)=3>0$. If $a\le0$, $\varphi'>0$ on $[0,1)$. If $a>0$, $\varphi$ increases up to $t=\dfrac{3}{2a}$ and decreases after it; it is one-one on $[0,1)$ exactly when $\dfrac{3}{2a}\ge1$, i.e. $a\le\dfrac32$. For $a>\dfrac32$ the vertex lies inside $(0,1)$ and values just below the maximum are taken twice, so such $a$ fail.

Between blocks: for $a\le\dfrac32$, $\varphi$ increases from $\varphi(0)=0$ towards $\varphi(1^{-})=3-a$, so block $n$ gives exactly the values $x\in[2n,\ 2n+3-a)$. Block $n+1$ gives $[2n+2,\ 2n+5-a)$.

These are disjoint for every $n$ if and only if $2n+3-a\le 2n+2$, i.e. $a\ge1$. If $a<1$, the number $x=2n+2$ is obtained both from $y=n+1$ and from some $y\in(n,n+1)$, so the vertical line $x=2n+2$ meets $R_a$ twice.
originality_note: New: a relation built from [y] and {y} with a parameter; the vertical line test splits into a within-block monotonicity condition (a <= 3/2) and a between-block non-overlap condition (a >= 1) (way 5, new combination). Closest known: equations of the form [x] + a{x} = c and graphs of [x], {x}. Different because: the student must read the vertical line test as injectivity of a piecewise map and find two opposite bounds from two different reasons.

concept_use.Definition of a function; vertical line: The vertical line test: R_a is a function of x exactly when y -> 2[y] + 3{y} - a{y}^2 is one-one, which gives the two conditions on a.
concept_use.Standard functions and their graphs (pol: The graphs of [y] and {y}: on each block [n, n+1) the map is 2n + 3t - at^2, so the block ranges [2n, 2n + 3 - a) decide the overlap.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and the domain of every function introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with code by an independent route, unique and equal to the plan. Checked numerically that a = 1, 1.2, 1.5 pass and a = 0.99, 1.6 fail (counting solutions y for a grid of x). Changed: No change.
key_step: Splitting the vertical line test into injectivity inside each block of [y] (a <= 3/2) and disjointness of the block ranges (a >= 1).
justification: Two independent conditions must be found and combined, one of which (block overlap) is easily missed; numerical answer with no options. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q6 (L3), a GIF-based function analysed piece by piece.
